newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page- April 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page- April 17.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Thursday:

* Top U.S. cigarette makers have begun talks which could lead to a settlement involving stricter government regulation, the formation of a large fund to cover the costs of smoking-related disease and advertising curbs.
* Israel's police minister said officers probing influence-peddling allegations in the Israeli government have recommended bringing charges against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

* The Chancellor of the Jewish Theological Seminary called for the dismantling of Israel's chief rabbinate and for the termination of contributions to groups opposed to recognising non-Orthodox movements in Israel.
* Republicans say there is nothing improper about a large dinner they are planning next month to draw donors who could give or raise as much as $250,000 each.
* New York City apartment residents are preparing for Monday's possible strike of janitors, doormen, elevator operators and handymen.
* Mining executives are signing remunerative deals in Zaire's Shaba province despite the country's uncertain future.
* The eastern German economy remains troubled, despite all the money western Germany has given it.

* News Analysis: Prosecutors in the Oklahoma City bombing case have weathered a number of setbacks, most recently the Justice Department inspector general's criticism of the Federal Bureau of Investigation's laboratory.
